subject: biology
title: Trophic levels and pyramids of biomass (Separate science)
key_idea: Organisms in a food chain are placed in trophic levels, starting with the producers. A pyramid of biomass shows the biomass at each level. Biomass falls at each step because some is lost through egestion, excretion and respiration.

blocks.text: (Separate science) A food chain shows what eats what. This section covers how each organism is placed in a trophic level.

items.meaning: The position of an organism in a food chain, numbered from level 1 at the start.
The mass of living material in organisms.

rows: Makes food by photosynthesis, using light absorbed by chlorophyll

blocks.text: An apex predator is a carnivore at the top of the chain with no predators. Decomposers break down dead plants and animals.

diagram.alt: Tap each role in a food chain to learn what it does.
diagram.prompt: Tap a role to see where it fits in a food chain, then test yourself.

parts.name: Producer
parts.detail: Makes its own food by photosynthesis. It is trophic level 1, at the start of every food chain.

parts.name: Primary consumer
parts.detail: A herbivore that eats the producers. It is trophic level 2.

parts.name: Secondary consumer
parts.detail: A carnivore that eats primary consumers. It is trophic level 3.

parts.name: Tertiary consumer
parts.detail: A carnivore that eats secondary consumers. It is trophic level 4.

parts.name: Apex predator
parts.detail: A carnivore with no predators, at the top of the food chain.

parts.name: Decomposer
parts.detail: Breaks down dead plant and animal material. This returns materials to the environment.

items: Producers are level 1. Consumers follow in order: primary, secondary, tertiary.
Producers get their energy from light by photosynthesis.

blocks.text: A pyramid of biomass shows how much biomass there is at each trophic level. This section covers how to draw one.

items.text: List the trophic levels from the producer to the top consumer.
Choose a scale so that the widest bar fits the page.
Draw one bar for each level. Make its width in proportion to the biomass at that level.
Put the producers at the bottom, and label each bar with the organism.

blocks.text: Each bar is narrower than the one below it, because biomass falls at each trophic level. This gives the pyramid shape.

items: A pyramid of biomass has one bar per trophic level, with the producers at the bottom.
Bar widths are in proportion to biomass.

sections.heading: Why biomass is lost between levels

blocks.text: Not all of the biomass at one level reaches the next. This section covers the ways it is lost.

items.meaning: Removing undigested material from the gut, as faeces.
Removing waste made by the body, such as urea and carbon dioxide.

items: **Not all of an organism is eaten.** Parts such as bones or shells are left.
**Egestion**: some of what is eaten is not digested or absorbed.
**Excretion**: urea in urine and carbon dioxide breathed out.
**Respiration** breaks down glucose and releases carbon dioxide. The energy released is used for movement and keeping warm, and is lost as heat.
Dead material is broken down by decomposers.

blocks.text: Animals that keep a constant body temperature, such as seals, lose more heat. They use more food, so less of it becomes biomass.
Because biomass falls at every level, there is too little left to support many more. This limits the length of a food chain.

items: Biomass is lost through uneaten parts, egestion, excretion and respiration.
This is why each trophic level has less biomass than the one below.

checks.q: In the food chain algae → invertebrate animals → small fish → large fish, name the producer and the secondary consumer.
checks.a: Producer: algae. Secondary consumer: small fish.

checks.q: Give two ways biomass is lost between trophic levels.
checks.a: Any two from: not all of the organism is eaten, egestion (faeces), excretion (urea, carbon dioxide), respiration.

checks.q: Describe how to draw a pyramid of biomass.
checks.a: Draw one bar for each trophic level in order, with the producers at the bottom. Make each bar's width in proportion to its biomass, using a scale, and label each bar.

worked_example.question:
Frogs also eat large beetles.

Give two reasons why only some of the energy in the biomass of the large beetles is transferred to the biomass of the frog.
answer_points: Not all of the beetle is eaten.
Not all of the beetle can be digested.
Energy is transferred to the surroundings as heat.
worked_example.tip: Any two score one mark each. "Maintaining body temperature" is ignored here.

worked_example.question: Write down two ways that biomass is lost from the food chain.
answer_points: Any two from: egestion (faeces or undigested food), excretion (a named excretory product or urine), respiration, decomposition, uneaten parts.

worked_example.question:
A student recorded information about an aquatic habitat.

Aquatic plants provide food for freshwater shrimps and midges. Mayflies also feed on aquatic plants. The mayflies provide food for salmon. Stoneflies feed on midges and are eaten by salmon. Salmon also eat freshwater shrimps. Herons feed on salmon.

Complete the table by naming the missing trophic levels and giving one organism at each different trophic level.

producer: aquatic plants
primary consumer: ______
secondary consumer: ______
______: ______
______: ______
answer_points: Primary consumer: mayflies, midges or freshwater shrimps.
worked_example.tip: One mark for a correct primary and a correct secondary consumer, one for tertiary consumer with an organism, one for quaternary consumer with an organism.

blocks.text: Some food chains have a fourth consumer. It eats the tertiary consumers and is called a **quaternary consumer**.

items: A pyramid of numbers has one bar for each trophic level.
The length of each bar is in proportion to the number of organisms at that level.
It can differ from a pyramid of biomass: one large tree can feed thousands of insects, so a bar can be shorter than the one above it.
A pyramid of biomass is more reliable. Mass allows for the size of organisms, and it never gives an inverted shape.
(Supplement) A pyramid of energy has one bar for each trophic level.
(Supplement) Each bar is in proportion to the energy at that level, for example in kJ per m² per year.
(Supplement) It is always a pyramid shape, because energy is lost as heat at each level.

worked_example.question:
This food chain is found in a food web.

microscopic algae → limpet → lobster → common seal

Explain why the amount of energy available to the organisms changes along this food chain.
answer_points: Energy is lost between each level.
It is lost as heat, or used in respiration or movement.
Some material is not eaten, not digested or is egested (faeces).
worked_example.tip: Any three different ways energy is lost score the marks.

blocks.text: The course also asks for pyramids of number and pyramids of energy.

items: A pyramid of numbers has one bar for each trophic level. Each bar is in proportion to the number of organisms.
It can differ from a pyramid of biomass: one large tree can feed thousands of insects, so a bar can be shorter than the one above it.
A pyramid of energy has one bar for each level, in proportion to the energy transferred. Energy is lost as heat at each level, so it is always a pyramid shape.
